title: Space Invaders
summary: The classic descending formation — but the twist is structural: the game orchestrator is itself a hierarchical state machine. $Playing, $PlayerDying, and $WaveComplete are all children of one $InGame parent that owns the shared pause/quit handlers, while a Fleet marches the formation and speeds up as its ranks thin.
teaches: Orchestrator-as-HSM: $InGame parent shares handlers across three combat sub-states via => $^ · a Fleet system marching a formation · push$/pop$ pause from inside the HSM
controls: A/D or ←/→ move · hold SPACE fire · P pause · SPACE start · R restart

machines.title: Invaders — the orchestrator (itself an HSM)
machines.blurb: $Attract → $InGame → $GameOver, where $InGame is a PARENT state: $Playing / $PlayerDying / $WaveComplete are its children and inherit its pause() and quit() handlers via => $^. The first game in the collection whose top-level controller is hierarchical, not flat — pause is a push$/pop$ interrupt reachable from any combat sub-state.

machines.title: Fleet — marching the formation
machines.blurb: $Marching → $Stepping → $Marching, with $Defeated as the terminal. The fleet owns the formation's descent cadence — it marches horizontally, drops and reverses at the edges, and accelerates as invaders are cleared. The scene owns the grid of sprites; the Fleet owns the rhythm.

machines.title: Player — hit/invulnerability window
machines.blurb: $Alive → $Exploding → $Invulnerable → $Alive (or $Dead) — the same damage loop as Shooter's player, with the invulnerability grace window as a timed state the orchestrator reads to decide $PlayerDying vs $GameOver.
